chunks: O People of the Book, Our Messenger has come to you, making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Book and pardoning much. There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Jews and Christians)
key_terms.رَسُولُنَا: Our Messenger (referring to Prophet Muhammad SAWW)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'light and a clear Book' sent to the People of the Book?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (SAWW) role in restoring the pristine truth of previous scriptures by clarifying the 'tahrif' (alteration/concealment) practiced by the Jews and Christians, while demonstrating divine mercy by overlooking other discrepancies. The mention of 'Nur' (Light) and 'Kitab' (Book) is often interpreted by scholars as referring to the Prophet and the Quran respectively, or collectively to the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing the clarity of guidance against the obscurity of prior traditions. This serves as a theological bridge, validating the continuity of revelation while asserting the finality and perfection of the Islamic message.
